summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for worsening fatigue, dyspnea, and abdominal distention. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with elevated BNP and mild volume overload. He was treated with intravenous diuresis, transitioned to torsemide, and achieved euvolemia. An echocardiogram showed normal systolic function but a small to moderate pericardial effusion without tamponade, likely related to heart failure or a mild viral process. A mildly elevated troponin was attributed to Type 2 myocardial infarction due to demand ischemia, with no evidence of acute coronary occlusion on stress testing. His apixaban dose was reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily due to decreased renal function, and transplant medications were continued unchanged. He improved clinically, was discharged home with close follow-up, and advised to monitor weight and symptoms.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
